I've written the storage design page and a brief for its first build step. Nothing was built or changed in the code; it's all committed and linked from the Page and JSONL readmes.

### 🗄️ The design `core/Page/doc/storage.md`
[/framework/core/Page/md/doc/storage/](/framework/core/Page/md/doc/storage/)

```
Page ─ page.store ─▶ Store (Item.Store, exists, keeps its methods)
  backend: DevBackend · StaticBackend · MemoryBackend · CloudBackend (later)
Journal, the page's home on a server:
  FileJournal (page.jsonl, the default) · RoomJournal (one Durable Object per page)
  D1Journal (lists across visitor pages) · Archive (E:, R2, Drive)
Index: in memory, beside the Journals, rebuilt from the JSONL files
```

- **Biggest decisions:**
  - Each kind of storage plugs into the one existing `Store` rather than getting its own subclass. Otherwise every storage kind would need its own page version.
  - Every page has exactly one place that accepts writes; every other copy is read-only.
  - The session index stays in memory, as you preferred; SQLite is kept only as a fallback.
- **Cost:** $0 a month at today's volume (142k log lines in 30 days), using Cloudflare prices fetched today. It becomes $5 if the deploy needs Workers Paid. A Durable Object costs about half a cent per hour it is awake and nothing while it sleeps.
- **Durable Object per page:** what costs money is how long objects stay awake, not how many there are. So one per live page is the right size, and it matches the 2026-09 …
